Event: `430504322e52c818510169e963cf356d` · 2026-10-03T06:19:43Z

> Several harts: how parallel a budget is, and the targets
> 
> 1. Should a budget run on at most one hart at a time? Recommended: yes. Different budgets run in parallel, but one budget's threads (a session's, a beamlet VM's) never run on two harts at once. K16 already flushes the whole TLB on every address-space switch, so a process's translations then exist only on the hart running it. That removes TLB shootdowns from unmap, lend and reply altogether. The only remote step left is evicting a budget that is being destroyed while it runs elsewhere, before its frames are freed. Freed frames now carry the free list's links, so that eviction is what keeps the kernel whole. The stride arithmetic keeps one runner per budget and stays unchanged. The alternative lets one budget use many harts: every unmap, lend and reply then needs IPI shootdowns (and ASIDs back), and charging and the floor need concurrent accounting. That is more kernel code and more to audit. It can be added later if a workload needs one budget on several harts.
>    - One hart per budget (recommended) (recommended): Budgets run in parallel; one budget never runs on two harts at once; no TLB shootdown protocol, only eviction at destruction.
>    - A budget's threads on many harts: Full IPI shootdowns on unmap, lend and reply, ASIDs per process, and concurrent stride accounting per budget.
> 2. For which hart counts are the latency targets (deadline notice 40 ms, R10 30 ms, a lease's end 125 ms, and the rest in scheduling.md) stated and gated? Recommended: they stay as they are and must hold at 1 and 2 harts; 4 harts is measured and recorded, not gated. The kernel takes one big FIFO lock: a hart can wait behind up to N-1 kernel sections, so at 4 harts a 22 ms destruction on two other harts could push a wake past 40 ms. Gating 4 harts would pull finer locking (step 5) into M2. If 2 harts miss a target, that is a finding against the kernel, as at the gate.
>    - 1 and 2 harts gated; 4 recorded (recommended) (recommended): Targets unchanged; SMP2 gates them at 1 and 2 harts and records 4.
>    - 1, 2 and 4 harts gated: Likely needs finer locking (step 5) within M2.
>    - 1 hart only, more harts recorded: Targets hold for one hart; several harts measured but not gated.

Event: `a7cc7f73e3f6b0ea64ab9ca6937ace72` · 2026-10-03T07:01:08Z

> Today, for K16: no path needs ASIDs, so K16's commit 3 (ASID 0 in satp) proceeds. With ASID 0 and a full flush at every satp switch, a hart holds translations only of the process it is running now. So the harts that must flush when a mapping leaves process P are exactly the harts currently running P, which each hart's per-hart block already records. ASIDs would widen that set to "every hart that ran P since its last flush", which is more state to audit. They come back only as a measured performance change.
> 
> Detail: .wash/local/SMP1-multihart.md. A multi-hart budget takes:
> - shootdowns to the other harts running the process, at every mapping removal (the eviction's lock-free acknowledgement, generalised);
> - remote fence.i for executable mappings and for threads that move;
> - a pick that lets several harts run one budget;
> - R12 restated across harts, with several runners per budget (the stride crate, the model and the mutations);
> - the big lock unchanged, so Q2 stands.
> 
> I recommend path A: designed for many harts, built in order. SMP1 as briefed, with its eviction built as a shootdown to a set of harts; SMP3 (M) puts a budget on several harts; SMP2 last, so R12 across harts is written and modelled once, with a case running the VM's two schedulers on two harts. Nothing gets built and then removed. The alternatives are B (one L+ package) and C (one hart per budget, which does not meet the goal). I am asking the owner now by decision_request on this thread. SMP1 stays blocked until they answer.

Event: `2d818ccafbc2931bbae23fa85b06b65a` · 2026-10-03T07:01:25Z

> Several harts: a beamlet VM on several harts at once
> 
> 1. Yes, a beamlet VM can run on several harts; beamlet already runs two scheduler threads. It needs one budget on several harts at once, which takes: TLB shootdowns to the other harts running the process whenever it loses a mapping (unmap, lend, reply); instruction fences when code is mapped or a thread moves harts; a scheduler that lets several harts run one budget, with R12 restated across harts (no gain from being spread). No ASIDs are needed (K16's flush at every switch keeps it exact). The big lock stays, so your answer on the targets stands. My estimate is 150-300 more kernel lines to audit than one hart per budget. Detail: .wash/local/SMP1-multihart.md. How should it be built?
>    - Many harts by design, three packages (recommended) (recommended): SMP1 (L) as briefed, with the destruction's eviction built as a shootdown to a set of harts; a budget stays on one hart only until SMP3. SMP3 (M): a budget on several harts. SMP2 (M-L) last: R12 and the targets across harts done once, plus a case running the VM's two schedulers on two harts. Nothing built is later removed.
>    - Many harts in one package: The same code, as SMP1 at size L+ then SMP2. Fewer packages, but one first merge too large to review well.
>    - One hart per budget for now: The earlier recommendation: least kernel code now, but a VM never uses two harts at once. Lifting it later adds SMP3 and redoes SMP2's fairness work.
